full_judgment:
2. The short fact relevant for disposal of the rule is that the petitioner as plaintiff brought the aforesaid Other Class Suit No.15 of 2007 before the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Badargonj, Rangpur impleading the opposite parties as defendants for permanent injunction on the averments that the suit land was originally belonged to Sree Profullo Prova Biswas in 16 annas share, who on 5-9-1961 executed a deed of power of Attorney in favour of his nephew Narayon Chandra Biswas. The said Narayon Chandra Biswas transferred 2.25 acres of land to Momtaz and Mokbul by registered Deed No. 34938 dated 28-11-1961. After the dead of Momtaz the heirs of Momtaz and Mokbul sold the entire 2.11 acres of land to the plaintiff vide deed No. 4857 dated 21-6-2004, The plaintiff has been possessing the suit land by growing paddy and various crops since purchase. The defendant attempted on 4-3-2007 to disposes the plaintiff from the suit properties and hence, this suit. 

 3. Immediately, after institution of the suit the plaintiff-petitioner filed an application for temporary injunction restraining defendants from disturbing with the peaceful possession of the plaintiff-petitioner in the suit property. 

 4. The learned Senior Assistant Judge, Badargonj, Rangpur after hearing by his order dated 3-4-2007 granted temporary injunction in favour of the plaintiff. Against which the defendants preferred Misc. Appeal No.34 of 2007 before the learned District Judge, Rangpur which was subsequently transferred to the Court of Joint District Judge, 3rd Court, Rangpur, who by the impugned judgment and order dated 29-7-2008 dismissed the appeal and affirmed the order of the trial Court below on the finding that prima-facie arguable case, balance of convenience and inconvenience is in favour of the plaintiff side 'and, as such, the trial Court below committed no wrong in granting temporary injunction in favour of the plaintiff and the said order was affirmed by the judgment and order of this Court dated 6-7-2009 passed in Civil Revision No.3752 of 2008. 

 5. In this backdrop, the plaintiff-petitioner on 5-10-2009 filed an application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure before the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Badargonj, Rangpur for appointment of police force. 

 6. The learned Senior Assistant Judge, Badargonj, Rangpur by his order dated 25-10-2009 rejected the said application and then again the plaintiff-petitioner on 24-11-2009 finding no other way filed an application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for appointment of police force in order to prevent the defendants from disturbing with the peaceful possession of the plaintiff in the suit property according to order of this Court. 

 9. Being aggrieved thereby the plaintiff-petitioner moved this Court and obtained the present Rule. 

 10. Mr Md lqbal Hossain, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that the Revisional Court below without applying its judicial mind into the facts and circumstances of the case and the case made out by the petitioner most illegally set-aside the well founded order of the trial Court dated 25-11-2009 which resulted in the failure of justice. He further submits that the trial Court on the facts of the case and on consideration of the legal position was perfectly justified in allowing the prayer for deployment of police force with a direction to the plaintiff to bear the costs although the revisional Court below completely overlooked the facts that the trial court granted temporary injunction in favour of the plaintiff which was affirmed by this Court and the petitioner finding no other way filed an application for appointment of police force stating if police is not deployed the defendants will evict the petitioner from the suit property and passed the impugned judgment on the wrong finding that the case is of civil nature the use of police force is not the efficacious remedy rather the learned Court below ought to have imposed civil remedy in taking action against the defendants in case of any violation of the temporary injunction and the same has occasioned failure of justice. 

 13. Now, to appreciate the submission of the learned Advocates from a correct angle at the very outset, I like to quote hereunder the relevant portion of the application filed by the plaintiff-petitioner under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for appointment of police force, which reads as follows: 

 14. Reading the application as a whole it appears that the defendant opposite parties after being unsuccessful up to this Court in an injunction matter became furious to disturb the plaintiff side in all possible manner ignoring the order of injunction. 

 17. It is a matter of discretion of the Court whether it is necessary to grant the prayer for appointment of police force in the compelling circumstances. In this case, I have already noticed that the trial Court factually found the possession of the plaintiff in the suit land and granted injunction in favour of the plaintiff which was affirmed up to this Court in Civil Revision No.3752 of 2008 vide judgment and order dated 6-7-2009. The trial Court on the facts of the case and on consideration of the legal position allowed the prayer for appointment of police force to avoid multiplicity of problems. In a suit of this nature the Court is quite competent to pass such order in applying its discretionary power, I find nothing wrong in the trail Court's finding. 

 18. On an overall consideration of the facts, circumstances and the materials on record I am of the view that the learned District Judge failed to consider the compelling circumstances leading to the filing of the application for appointment of police force in the suit property by the plaintiff-petitioner and thus fell into an error of law in setting aside the order of the trial Court dated 6-7-2009 and the same has occasioned a failure of justice. In the conclusion, I find no difficulty whatever in holding that the learned District Judge, Rangpur was plainly wrong in setting aside the order of the trail court dated 25-11-2009 on the finding that "the case is of civil nature the use of police force is not the efficacious remedy rather the learned Court below ought to have imposed civil remedy in taking action against the defendants in case of any violation of the temporary injunction". Therefore, I find considerable merit in the aforesaid submission of the learned Advocate, Mr Md Iqbal Hossain.
